executive_summary: Fixes the quick_fixes claim-eviction race: claim_sd resets an evicted row to open (or refuses if mid-CI) atomically, and worker-checkin's three self-claim paths uniformly skip self-claim via getMyClaims().

functional_requirements.requirement: claim_sd's claim-switch eviction path resets an evicted quick_fixes row's status to 'open' in the SAME guarded UPDATE that clears claiming_session_id.
functional_requirements.description: database/migrations/20260903_claim_sd_symmetric_clear_returning_fix.sql lines 474-478 (the `IF v_evicted_sd_key LIKE 'QF-%' THEN UPDATE quick_fixes SET claiming_session_id = NULL WHERE id = v_evicted_sd_key` branch) must add `status = 'open'` to that SET clause. Does NOT apply to the strategic_directives_v2 branch immediately below it (lines ~479-486) -- that table has no 'open' status value in its CHECK constraint (verified live) and already correctly clears claiming_session_id/active_session_id/is_working_on with no orphan shape.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Evicting a quick_fixes claim with no pr_url/commit_sha leaves the row with status='open', claiming_session_id=NULL, queryable immediately after the evicting claim_sd call returns.

AC-2: The reset and the clear happen in the SAME UPDATE statement (not a follow-up UPDATE by id), so a third session's fresh legitimate claim landing between two statements can never be stomped back to 'open'.
AC-3: The strategic_directives_v2 eviction branch is unchanged byte-for-byte except for this SD's other additions.

functional_requirements.requirement: claim_sd refuses (touches nothing, returns a refusal code) when the quick_fixes row being evicted carries a non-null pr_url or commit_sha.
functional_requirements.description: Express the refusal as a predicate directly on the destructive UPDATE's WHERE clause (`AND pr_url IS NULL AND commit_sha IS NULL`) plus a GET DIAGNOSTICS row-count check -- matching this same migration's own existing pattern for v_evicted_row_count (line 470-473) -- never a separate prior SELECT+branch, because READ COMMITTED with no FOR UPDATE means a prior read can go stale before the write executes.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A quick_fixes row with pr_url set is NOT evicted by a competing claim_sd call; the row's status and claiming_session_id are unchanged.
AC-2: The same holds for commit_sha set with pr_url NULL (tested as a distinct case).
AC-3: claim_sd's return shape carries a distinguishable refusal code/reason the caller (worker-checkin.cjs) can branch on, not a silent no-op.

functional_requirements.requirement: worker-checkin.cjs's three self-claim producer steps (critical-qf-jump.cjs, merged-pool-self-claim.cjs, self-claim-qf.cjs) all skip self-claim when the calling session already authoritatively holds ANY live claim (SD or QF).
functional_requirements.description: Apply lib/claim/get-my-claims.cjs's getMyClaims(supabase, sessionId) -- the existing authoritative both-kinds, multiplicity-aware predicate, currently called only from resume.cjs -- to all three producer steps uniformly. Do NOT key the guard on ctx.mySd: it is a one-shot mirror snapshot nulled at multiple points in the same pipeline (resume.cjs:147, resume.cjs:229, release-request.cjs:117), so a guard keyed on it is inert in exactly the race this SD exists to fix.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A session already holding a live SD claim does not self-claim a QF from self-claim-qf.cjs's self_claimed_qf tier.
AC-2: A session already holding a live QF claim does not self-claim an SD from critical-qf-jump.cjs or merged-pool-self-claim.cjs.
AC-3: All three producer steps call the SAME getMyClaims() import -- no duplicated/reimplemented ownership check.

functional_requirements.requirement: Investigate what happens today when a directed-assignment claim attempt is REJECTED by claim_sd, and fix the fall-through if the pipeline does not correctly resolve to self-claim afterward.
functional_requirements.description: Assignment already outranks self-claim in the existing worker-checkin.cjs step ordering, so a guard merely restating that ordering is a no-op -- the real unknown is the REJECTION path specifically: does a rejected assigned-claim attempt correctly fall through to the self-claim tiers, or does it leave the pipeline stuck having already skipped them for this tick? This is an investigation-first requirement; implement a fix only if the investigation finds a genuine gap.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A documented trace (code reading + a reproducing test) of the current rejected-assignment fall-through behavior exists.
AC-2: If a gap is found, the pipeline resolves to a self-claim (or a correctly-reported idle/error state) after a rejected assignment, never a silent no-action tick.
AC-3: If no gap is found, the investigation's finding is recorded in the PRD/handoff evidence rather than producing speculative code changes.

functional_requirements.requirement: A seat sleeping on a claim-wakeup (wind_down.had_claim=true) whose claim is removed by someone else receives a hint it can act on at its NEXT check-in.
functional_requirements.description: Matches the existing precedent at scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs:352-366. This SD does NOT attempt to preempt or re-arm an already-scheduled ScheduleWakeup mid-sleep -- that capability does not exist in the harness and is already formally risk-accepted (docs/.../fleet-hibernation-quiet-tick.md:159-171, lib/fleet/self-wake-escalation.cjs:15-22). The fix is purely a hint written at removal time and read at the seat's own next check-in.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A park/release action on a had_claim=true-sleeping seat's claim writes a hint record.
AC-2: The seat's next /checkin call surfaces and can act on that hint.
AC-3: No new wake-preemption mechanism is introduced.

functional_requirements.requirement: Every claim_sd eviction-with-reset and every eviction-refusal emits a queryable structured audit event.
functional_requirements.description: Follow this same migration file's existing event_type='CLAIM_SWITCH_EVICTED_CLEARED' pattern (session_lifecycle_events INSERT gated on the clear actually firing) as the template: add a distinct event_type for the quick_fixes reset-on-evict case and another for the pr_url/commit_sha refusal case. Verification of this SD's effect must use these events, never a standing orphan-row COUNT -- the live orphan count is already 0 (the defect is racy/intermittent, not a steady population), so a count-based check would read as permanently healthy whether or not the fix is present.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: An eviction-with-reset (FR-1) inserts a session_lifecycle_events row identifying the evicted quick_fixes id and the evicting session.
AC-2: An eviction-refusal (FR-2) inserts a session_lifecycle_events row identifying the refused id and the reason (pr_url/commit_sha present).
AC-3: Both event types are queryable after the fact and distinguishable from the existing CLAIM_SWITCH_EVICTED_CLEARED event.

functional_requirements.requirement: No regression to QF-20260912-961's already-shipped parts (a) and (b).
functional_requirements.description: LEO_RELEASE_WORKITEM_RESET (lib/fleet/release-work-item.mjs:134, verified live) must still default ON ('off' remains the only kill switch), and the quick_fixes phantom-in_progress detector in scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs (verified live at lines 3086-3127, delegating to releaseWorkItemOnSessionEnd() at line 3113-3114) must still delegate to that shared helper with no duplicated reopen predicate.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Existing stale-session-sweep-workitem-handback.test.js and sibling QF-961 regression tests pass unmodified.
AC-2: No new code path reimplements releaseWorkItemOnSessionEnd()'s reopen logic.

technical_requirements.requirement: The claim_sd migration expresses both the reset (FR-1) and the refusal (FR-2) as predicates and GET DIAGNOSTICS row-count checks directly on the single destructive UPDATE statement, never as a prior SELECT followed by a branching UPDATE.
technical_requirements.rationale: The database runs READ COMMITTED with no FOR UPDATE row lock on this path (confirmed by this same migration file's own v_evicted_row_count pattern, added for the identical reason at lines 41/470-473) -- a prior SELECT can go stale before the write executes, reintroducing exactly the race class this migration file already exists to close.

technical_requirements.requirement: lib/claim/get-my-claims.cjs's getMyClaims(supabase, sessionId) is imported identically (same module path, same call signature) into critical-qf-jump.cjs, merged-pool-self-claim.cjs, and self-claim-qf.cjs -- no per-file reimplementation of the ownership predicate.
technical_requirements.rationale: A second, slightly-different hand-rolled ownership check in any one producer step is how this exact bug class regresses silently -- the predicate must stay single-sourced so a future fix to getMyClaims() reaches all three call sites automatically.

technical_requirements.requirement: The new audit events (FR-6) reuse the existing session_lifecycle_events table and insert pattern already present in this migration file, adding new event_type literals rather than a new table or sink.
technical_requirements.rationale: session_lifecycle_events is already the canonical durable-trail sink for claim-lifecycle events in this codebase (the CLAIM_SWITCH_EVICTED_CLEARED precedent in the same file); a second sink would fragment the audit trail this SD's own success criteria depend on for verification.

technical_requirements.requirement: The migration is additive and backward compatible: existing callers of claim_sd (worker-checkin.cjs's multiple call sites) continue to work unchanged against the new function signature/behavior, with no caller-side code required to adopt the reset/refusal behavior.
technical_requirements.rationale: claim_sd is called from numerous call sites across the fleet-worker checkin pipeline; a signature or return-shape change that requires every caller to be updated in lockstep would turn a small, low-risk fix into a fleet-wide breaking change.

system_architecture.overview: A Postgres RPC function (claim_sd) mediates every SD/QF claim and claim-switch in the fleet. worker-checkin.cjs's three self-claim producer steps call it when a session has no directed assignment. This SD tightens claim_sd's eviction branch for quick_fixes (reset-on-evict, refuse-if-mid-CI) and adds a single shared pre-check (getMyClaims) across the three producer steps so a session that already holds a claim never races itself into a second one.

components.name: claim_sd (Postgres function)
components.responsibility: Atomically claims/evicts SD and QF rows; this SD adds a status reset and a refusal predicate to its quick_fixes eviction branch.

components.name: lib/claim/get-my-claims.cjs
components.responsibility: Authoritative, both-kinds (SD+QF) predicate for 'does this session already hold a live claim' -- applied uniformly to all three self-claim producer steps.

components.name: worker-checkin.cjs self-claim producer steps (critical-qf-jump.cjs, merged-pool-self-claim.cjs, self-claim-qf.cjs)
components.responsibility: Each calls getMyClaims() before attempting a self-claim; skip if the session already holds any live claim.

components.name: session_lifecycle_events
components.responsibility: Durable audit sink; receives a new event_type on every eviction-with-reset and every eviction-refusal.

components.name: scripts/stale-session-sweep.cjs (hint writer)
components.responsibility: Writes a next-checkin hint when a sleeping seat's claim is removed out from under it, matching the existing precedent at lines 352-366.

system_architecture.data_flow: worker-checkin.cjs calls claim_sd (RPC) when claiming an item. If the call evicts an existing quick_fixes claim, claim_sd checks pr_url/commit_sha on the evicted row: if both NULL, it resets status to 'open' and clears claiming_session_id in one UPDATE and emits an audit event; if either is set, it refuses, touches nothing, and emits a different audit event. Separately, each of the three self-claim producer steps calls getMyClaims() before attempting any self-claim RPC call, short-circuiting if the session already holds a live claim. A sleeping seat whose claim is removed gets a hint row it reads at its next /checkin.
integration_points: strategic_directives_v2 table (read-only for this SD; eviction branch unchanged)

test_scenarios.scenario: Evict a quick_fixes claim with no pr_url/commit_sha via a competing claim_sd call.
test_scenarios.given: Session A holds a quick_fixes claim with pr_url=NULL and commit_sha=NULL.
test_scenarios.when: Session B calls claim_sd to claim a different item, triggering the claim-switch eviction of A's claim.
test_scenarios.then: The evicted row reads status='open', claiming_session_id=NULL in the same transaction, and a CLAIM_EVICT_RESET (or equivalent) audit event is recorded.

test_scenarios.scenario: Attempt to evict a quick_fixes claim that carries a pr_url.
test_scenarios.given: Session A holds a quick_fixes claim with pr_url set.
test_scenarios.when: Session B calls claim_sd in a way that would otherwise evict A's claim.
test_scenarios.then: claim_sd returns a refusal; the row's status and claiming_session_id are unchanged; an audit event distinct from TS-1's is recorded.

test_scenarios.scenario: Attempt to evict a quick_fixes claim that carries a commit_sha but no pr_url.
test_scenarios.given: Session A holds a quick_fixes claim with pr_url=NULL and commit_sha set.
test_scenarios.when: Session B calls claim_sd in a way that would otherwise evict A's claim.
test_scenarios.then: Same refusal behavior as TS-2 -- commit_sha alone is sufficient to block eviction.

test_scenarios.scenario: A session already holding a live SD claim reaches the QF self-claim tier.
test_scenarios.given: Session C holds a live SD claim (confirmed via getMyClaims).
test_scenarios.when: self-claim-qf.cjs's self_claimed_qf tier runs for session C with an open QF available.
test_scenarios.then: Session C does not self-claim the QF; the tier short-circuits on getMyClaims() returning a live claim.

test_scenarios.scenario: A session already holding a live QF claim reaches an SD self-claim tier.
test_scenarios.given: Session D holds a live QF claim (confirmed via getMyClaims).
test_scenarios.when: critical-qf-jump.cjs or merged-pool-self-claim.cjs runs for session D with a claimable SD available.
test_scenarios.then: Session D does not self-claim the SD; both tiers short-circuit identically via the same getMyClaims() call.

test_scenarios.scenario: A directed-assignment claim attempt is rejected by claim_sd.
test_scenarios.given: Session E receives a directed WORK_ASSIGNMENT for an item that claim_sd rejects (e.g. already claimed elsewhere).
test_scenarios.then: The pipeline falls through to the self-claim tiers (or correctly reports an idle/error state) for that tick -- never a silent no-action tick (FR-4).

test_scenarios.scenario: QF-20260912-961 regression suite runs unmodified against the new claim_sd migration.
test_scenarios.given: The existing stale-session-sweep-workitem-handback.test.js and sibling QF-961 tests.
test_scenarios.when: The full suite runs after this SD's migration and code changes are applied.
test_scenarios.then: All QF-961 tests pass unmodified -- LEO_RELEASE_WORKITEM_RESET still defaults ON and the quick_fixes phantom-in_progress detector still delegates to releaseWorkItemOnSessionEnd().

acceptance_criteria: A quick_fixes claim evicted with no pr_url/commit_sha reads status='open' immediately after the evicting claim_sd call returns, with the reset and the clear performed in one UPDATE statement.
A quick_fixes claim carrying a pr_url or commit_sha is never evicted; claim_sd returns a refusal and the row is left completely untouched.
A session already holding a live claim (SD or QF, via getMyClaims) never self-claims a second item from any of the three self-claim producer steps.
Every eviction-with-reset and every eviction-refusal emits a distinguishable, queryable session_lifecycle_events row.
Existing QF-20260912-961 regression tests pass unmodified.

risks.risk: A migration written directly from the originating ticket text (pre-LEAD-correction) would attempt status='open' and pr_url/commit_sha predicates against strategic_directives_v2, which has no 'open' status value and no pr_url/commit_sha columns (both verified live) -- either silently no-op or hard-fail with 42703.
risks.mitigation: LEAD-phase prospective testing-agent review (evidence row 5d196f47-4555-4f50-998d-101d38a2ccef) caught this before PRD authoring; every FR above is explicitly scoped to quick_fixes only, and the strategic_directives_v2 eviction branch is called out as unchanged in FR-1.
risks.rollback_plan: No production exposure possible: the PRD itself enforces quick_fixes-only scope, so there is no strategic_directives_v2 migration path to roll back.

risks.risk: FR-5's 'next-checkin hint' could be mis-implemented as an attempt to preempt or re-arm an already-scheduled ScheduleWakeup mid-sleep, which has no implementation primitive in the harness.
risks.mitigation: FR-5 explicitly scopes the fix to a hint written at removal time and read at the seat's own next check-in, citing the existing formal risk-acceptance docs (fleet-hibernation-quiet-tick.md, self-wake-escalation.cjs) so EXEC does not re-open that decision under time pressure.
risks.rollback_plan: The hint write is a single additive INSERT/UPDATE with no behavioral coupling to ScheduleWakeup; reverting it is a straight revert of that one code change.

risks.risk: The new claim_sd migration could introduce a regression in an existing, frequently-exercised call path (claim_sd is called from numerous worker-checkin.cjs sites) if the new predicates are not additive.
risks.mitigation: TR-4 requires the migration to be additive and backward compatible; TS-7 runs the full QF-961 regression suite plus this SD's own new tests (TS-1..TS-6) before the migration is considered complete.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert via a down-migration restoring the prior claim_sd function body (pinned verbatim in git history at database/migrations/20260903_claim_sd_symmetric_clear_returning_fix.sql) -- a single CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION statement, no data migration involved.

phases.description: Author the claim_sd migration: add the status='open' reset (FR-1) and the pr_url/commit_sha refusal predicate (FR-2) to the quick_fixes eviction branch, plus the two new audit event types (FR-6).
deliverables: Unit/integration tests for TS-1, TS-2, TS-3

phases.description: Apply getMyClaims() uniformly to the three self-claim producer steps (FR-3).
deliverables: Guard added to critical-qf-jump.cjs, merged-pool-self-claim.cjs, self-claim-qf.cjs

phases.description: Investigate directed-assignment rejection fall-through (FR-4); implement a fix only if a gap is confirmed.
deliverables: Fix + TS-6 if needed, or a documented no-gap finding

phases.description: Add the next-checkin hint for a sleeping seat's removed claim (FR-5).
deliverables: Test confirming hint surfaces at next check-in

phases.description: Run the full QF-20260912-961 regression suite (FR-7/TS-7) and this SD's own new tests together before EXEC-TO-PLAN handoff.

technical_decisions: Scope the claim_sd changes to quick_fixes only -- strategic_directives_v2 has no 'open' status and no pr_url/commit_sha columns, verified live during LEAD phase.
Express eviction-reset and eviction-refusal as predicates + row-count checks on the single destructive UPDATE, not a prior SELECT+branch, given no row locking on this path.
Reuse getMyClaims() and session_lifecycle_events rather than introducing new ownership predicates or audit sinks.
Scope the sleeping-seat fix to a next-checkin hint only, explicitly declining to attempt ScheduleWakeup preemption (no implementation primitive exists).

consumers.name: Fleet worker sessions
consumers.interaction: Call claim_sd via worker-checkin.cjs on every check-in cycle to claim/switch SD and QF work items.

consumers.name: Coordinator
consumers.interaction: Reads session_lifecycle_events audit rows to observe eviction-reset and eviction-refusal events.

dependencies.name: claim_sd Postgres function
dependencies.contract: worker-checkin.cjs calls it as an RPC; this SD changes its internal eviction behavior without changing its external call contract (TR-4).
dependencies.failure_handling: A refusal returns a distinguishable code the caller already has to handle (claim contention is a normal, expected outcome of this RPC).

dependencies.name: lib/claim/get-my-claims.cjs
dependencies.contract: Imported identically by all three self-claim producer steps (TR-2).
dependencies.failure_handling: If getMyClaims() throws or errors, the producer step should fail closed (skip self-claim) rather than assume no existing claim.

data_contracts.schema: status, claiming_session_id, pr_url, commit_sha columns on quick_fixes
data_contracts.validation: Enforced inside the claim_sd migration's predicates (FR-1, FR-2)
data_contracts.versioning: Single additive migration; no version negotiation needed since callers are unaffected (TR-4).

runtime_config.deployment_considerations: Straight SQL migration + application code change; no feature flag per this SD's scope (unlike QF-20260912-961's LEO_RELEASE_WORKITEM_RESET precedent) since the new behavior is strictly additive and low-risk per the RISK sub-agent's LOW rating.

monitoring: session_lifecycle_events rows for the two new event_types (eviction-with-reset, eviction-refusal)
alerts: An unexpected spike in eviction-refusal events could indicate a claim-contention problem elsewhere in the fleet worth investigating.
observability_rollout.rollout_strategy: Single migration + code deploy; verified via TS-1..TS-7 before merge.
observability_rollout.rollback_trigger: Any QF-961 regression test failure, or a new test (TS-1..TS-6) failing post-deploy.
observability_rollout.rollback_procedure: Revert via a down-migration restoring the prior claim_sd function body, pinned verbatim in database/migrations/20260903_claim_sd_symmetric_clear_returning_fix.sql; revert the getMyClaims() guard commits independently if only Phase 2 regresses.

patterns_identified: claim_sd has two distinct eviction paths: a 'takeover' path (evicting a DIFFERENT session's claim on the SAME item) and a 'claim-switch'/'symmetric-clear' path (evicting the CALLING session's OWN prior claim on a DIFFERENT item) -- this SD's defect lives in the latter.

ctx.mySd is a one-shot mirror, not a durable guard key -- it is nulled at multiple points in the checkin pipeline (resume.cjs:147, :229, release-request.cjs:117), so any guard keyed on it is inert against the exact race this SD targets.
getMyClaims() is already the authoritative, both-kinds, multiplicity-aware claim-ownership predicate but is currently called only from resume.cjs, not from the other self-claim producer steps.
session_lifecycle_events already has a precedent (CLAIM_SWITCH_EVICTED_CLEARED) for a gated INSERT on a successful clear -- the correct template for this SD's new audit events rather than a new sink.
key_decisions: Scope c2/f to quick_fixes only after live-verifying strategic_directives_v2 has no 'open' status value and no pr_url/commit_sha columns.
Scope g (sleeping-seat handling) to a next-checkin hint only, per existing formal risk-acceptance that ScheduleWakeup preemption is not implementable.
Reframe c1 (directed-assignment) as an investigation-first requirement rather than an assumed fix, since the existing step ordering already makes a naive restated guard a no-op.
